_comment: Shared fixture for page-relative compass bearing. BOTH implementations
Every case here was worked out by hand from bearing.py's own convention
(0 = north = up on the image, clockwise, image y increases downward),
not captured from either implementation's output. Distances use
metresPerPx 1 unless a case says otherwise.
The 'argument order' cases exist because of the real bug this module was
built to fix: a live description read '270 m NW of General Hospital'
when it should have read SE -- bearingDeg(self, landmark) was being
phrased as if it were bearingDeg(landmark, self). Both directions of the
same pair are asserted here so a future regression trips on the fixture,
not on a player reading the wrong description.

cases.why: straight up on the image is north
straight down is south -- image y increases downward
a non-45-degree case, so this is not just testing the eight exact diagonals
metresPerPx actually scales the distance, not just the pixel count
the real incident, forward direction: the building is SE of the hospital
the real incident, reversed: the hospital is NW of the building -- the OPPOSITE reading, which is what the bug actually displayed
